sets.name: Section 01 Reading 1 손을 들어 모두, 샤카!
sents: If you ever visit Hawaii, the locals will probably greet you with an unusual hand gesture and the words “shaka brah.”
This warm welcome, known as the shaka, is popular throughout the islands.
From businessmen to surfers, everyone uses this friendly gesture.
It helps to promote peace and harmony among the wide range of ethnic groups living there.
No one is sure where the shaka first originated, but the most common theory is that it stems from beach culture.
The term shaka itself is probably a variation on the common expression “shark eye,” which is a compliment paid to show respect.
The shaka gesture became popular in the 1960s thanks to local celebrity Lippy Espinda, who used it in television advertisements.
From then on, everyone began using the shaka as a friendly show of goodwill.
Here’s how to make a shaka sign.
The first step is to make a fist.
Then extend your thumb and pinky, but be sure not to uncurl your middle fingers.
Then, turn your hand so that your palm is facing towards you.
Finally, move it as if writing the letter “J.”
That’s it.
Now you are ready to greet people the Hawaiian way!

sets.name: Section 01 Reading 2 보기만 해도 아찔해요!
sents: Legs trembling and palms sweaty, you ascend the stairs.
You are making your way toward Xuan Kong Si, also known as the Hanging Temple, in China.
Renowned for its location, the temple is ingeniously built into a cliff more than seventy-five meters above the ground.
Despite looking fragile, the Hanging Temple has remarkably been “hanging” there for about fifteen hundred years!
The secret is its unique architectural design, which includes slender wooden poles that are embedded in the rock and function as the foundation.
It is easy to assume that these poles play a key role in supporting the structure; however, the temple was actually constructed in a way that lets the rock face carry the majority of the weight.
The interior of the temple is just as distinct as its exterior.
The temple features forty chambers connected by narrow stairs and bridges.
It also integrates three religions—Buddhism, Taoism, and Confucianism—and is home to eighty-seven statues that honor these belief systems.
Why do you think the temple was built like this?
One reason is that the elevated location protects the temple from the floods of the nearby river.
Another is its tranquil setting, which creates an ideal place for meditation and the search for inner peace.
Ironically, this once-remote place has become a popular tourist attraction.
Would you dare to climb up to it?

sets.name: Section 01 Reading 3 ‘무’시’무’시한 축제
sents: As a beloved Halloween tradition, people in the United States carve scary faces into pumpkins to create jack-o’-lanterns.
But south of the border, in Oaxaca, Mexico, there is a different carving tradition that happens around Christmas instead of Halloween.
And rather than pumpkins, people carve radishes!
The celebration is called Noche de Rabanos, or Night of the Radishes, and it takes place on December 23.
It was started more than 100 years ago by merchants at the town plaza.
Hoping to attract Christmas shoppers, they would carve designs into the bright red skin of radishes.
People loved them!
They bought the carved radishes and placed them in the center of the table at Christmas dinner.
In 1897, Noche de Rabanos became an official holiday in Oaxaca.
Today, the carvings are made by local artists and amateurs.
They use special radishes that are larger than normal and not used for food.
These radishes, which can weigh as much as three kilograms, are harvested on December 18.
This gives the carvers a few days to work on their creations before exhibiting them in the town plaza.
The person who carves the best radish wins a grand prize of over 30,000 pesos.
If you’re ever in Mexico during the holiday season, you should head to Oaxaca and check out these wonderful Christmas radishes!

sets.name: Section 01 Reading 4 수능:ON 주제 · 제목
sents: In Romania, there is a surprising tourist attraction located 120 meters beneath the ground near the city of Turda.
The place was once a large salt mine that was dug by the Romans long ago.
Now, however, it has been turned into an underground museum and theme park!
Visitors can enter by taking an elevator or walking down a long tunnel.
The mine is about 12 degrees Celsius year round and the air’s humidity remains at approximately 80%.
What’s more, the air itself is very clean, with little dust or bacteria.
This makes the salt mine a great place for people with allergies!
The bottom of the mine, which is covered by a layer of salt, offers visitors many fun things to do.
There is a sports arena, a Ferris wheel, a bowling alley, and even a miniature golf course.
People can also check out the original mining equipment or rent a boat to take a tour of an underground lake.
The mine looks like something from a fairytale.
An interesting combination of old and new, the Turda salt mine is a great example of how places from the past can be brought back to life.

sets.name: Section 02 Reading 1 이 색, 무슨 소리야?
sents: Instead of dressing based on appearance, he selects outfits based on what “sounds” good.
He consumes pop songs as appetizers and piano sonatas as his main course.
This may seem peculiar, but this reflects how Neil Harbisson experiences the world on a daily basis.
Without a doubt, he is a truly unique person.
Born completely color blind, Harbisson could only perceive shades of gray.
However, meeting computer scientist Adam Montandon led to the development of an innovative device known as an eyeborg.
It functions as an electronic eye that Harbisson wears on his head.
Once it detects color frequencies, it changes them into sound frequencies.
This information is then sent to a chip at the back of Harbisson’s head.
The transmission of waves through his skull allows him to hear the sounds.
Consequently, for Harbisson, visiting an art gallery becomes an auditory experience comparable to attending a concert, while shopping at a supermarket parallels listening to a live DJ performance.
Remarkably, his eyeborg has made him even more sensitive to colors than someone with normal vision.
In addition to the millions of shades along the visible light spectrum, he can also detect invisible light such as ultraviolet.
Harbisson hopes to provide others with the access to similar devices.
He advocates expanding our natural senses by integrating them with technology.
He believes it can give us a new perspective on the world, making our lives much more exciting!

sets.name: Section 02 Reading 2 머리카락으로 밝힌 미스터리
sents: The composer Ludwig van Beethoven died on March 27, 1827.
Before his death, however, he expressed a desire for his health issues to be studied and shared with the public.
Recently, researchers set out to uncover more information on Beethoven’s health issues by conducting a DNA analysis of his hair.
One of their goals was to shed light on Beethoven’s hearing loss.
They also hoped to discover the primary cause of his death.
The analysis revealed that Beethoven suffered from lead poisoning near the end of his life.
According to the results, Beethoven’s lead levels were extremely high, likely because he drank wine sweetened with lead.
However, the researchers don’t think that his death was caused solely by lead poisoning, though it likely did contribute to his deafness and digestive issues.
The analysis also uncovered evidence that Beethoven dealt with a liver disease late in his life.
This was probably another contributing factor in his death.
In a letter he wrote, Beethoven admitted to feeling hopeless as a composer because of his hearing loss.
Yet he didn’t want to die until he had composed all the music he was inspired to make.
Every piece of information that we uncover about Beethoven provides insight into how he turned his pain into music.

sets.name: Section 02 Reading 3 길을 잃지 않는 마을
sents: Taking care of people with Alzheimer’s disease requires a lot of effort.
They tend to wander around a lot, and, because of their memory problems, they easily forget where they are.
That’s why Hogewey was established in the Netherlands in 2009.
Unlike typical nursing homes, it’s a whole village where residents can visit shops, cafés, restaurants, and even a movie theater.
And they have the freedom to wander around as much as they want!
Nurses and other employees wear normal clothes and behave like villagers.
So if residents get lost or confused, there’s always someone there to assist them.
Hogewey accommodates more than 180 residents and is staffed by about 250 employees.
Six to eight residents share each apartment in the village’s 27 residential buildings.
Surprisingly, the cost per resident is not that much higher than at traditional nursing homes.
Above all, Hogewey provides patients with a comfortable environment where they can enjoy some of the freedoms they had lost in their daily lives.
Moreover, Hogewey is changing how people think about Alzheimer’s by allowing its residents to live in a normal community.

sets.name: Section 02 Reading 4 수능:ON 요지 · 주장
sents: Take the choice of which kind of soup to buy.
There’s too much data here for you to struggle with: calories, price, salt content, taste, packaging, and so on.
If you were a robot, you would be stuck here all day trying to make a decision, with no obvious way to trade off which details matter more.
To land on a choice, you need a summary of some sort.
And that’s what the feedback from your body is able to give you.

Thinking about your budget might make your palms sweat, or your mouth might water thinking about the last time you consumed the chicken noodle soup, or noting the excessive creaminess of the other soup might give you a stomachache.
You simulate your experience with one soup, and then the other.
Your bodily experience helps your brain to quickly place a value on soup A and another on soup B, allowing you to tip the balance in one direction or the other.
You don’t just extract the data from soup cans, you feel the data.

sets.name: Section 03 Reading 1 크림 전쟁의 숨은 영웅
sents: Although Florence Nightingale is best known as the founder of modern nursing, she was also a skilled statistician.
Nightingale used statistics to figure out why so many people died in the Crimean War.
She then used this information effectively to change public opinion.
Nightingale was sent to a British hospital in Turkey in 1854 in order to improve its conditions.
Many injured soldiers were dying in the hospital, which was suffering from shortages of food and medicine, an overworked staff, and unclean conditions.
By the time the war ended in 1856, Nightingale and her team had successfully improved the hospital, significantly lowering the death rates of wounded soldiers.
Despite this success, Nightingale worried that similar situations would occur in the future.
So she used her abilities as a statistician to analyze the cause of hospital deaths during the war.
It was commonly believed that most of the deaths were due to shortages of food and medicine.
However, Nightingale found that the real cause was unsanitary conditions.
Nightingale was asked to present this information to the queen and her council.
She knew that simply reading a list of numbers wasn’t enough.
So she arranged the numbers into charts to make them clearer.
Charts weren’t commonly used in those days, but they had a powerful impact.
They convinced many people that something had to be done.
Thanks to Florence Nightingale’s statistical skills, public sanitation and the British hospital system were improved, saving countless lives.

sets.name: Section 03 Reading 2 전쟁 속의 또 다른 비극
sents: Many people view Winston Churchill as one of the greatest leaders of World War II.
As the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, he held his country together during difficult times and helped to lead the Allied Forces to victory.
But not everyone saw Churchill as a great man, especially not those living in areas colonized by the British Empire.
In fact, he is considered to be partially responsible for millions of deaths in Bengal, a region in northeastern India.
In 1943, Bengal was ruled by Britain and was suffering from a serious famine.
There was plenty of rice being grown in other parts of India, but most of it was being exported to feed British soldiers.
Not only did Churchill refuse to send some of this rice to Bengal, but he also turned down offers from the United States and Canada to provide food.
His reason was that he feared enemy soldiers who were near Bengal would take the food.
In the end, approximately 3 million people starved to death in Bengal.
Although Churchill had no way of preventing the famine, he could have reduced the number of victims.
Instead, he turned his back on the people of Bengal and let them die.
Because he coldly decided to put his country before human lives, some people view him as a heartless and cruel man.

sets.name: Section 03 Reading 3 ‘미친 척’이 만든 진짜 변화
sents: In 1887, 23-year-old Nellie Bly already had a career as a journalist in the small city of Pittsburgh.
However, most of the stories she was asked to write were directed only at women.
Bly dreamed of writing important stories for all readers, so she moved to New York and tried to find work at the New York World, which was one of the nation’s leading newspapers at that time.
The editor of the newspaper offered her a challenge.
He asked her to investigate a local mental hospital with a bad reputation for treating patients poorly.
In order to get inside, Bly pretended to be mentally ill for 10 days.
The story that she wrote about her experience was published as a six-part series, and it made her one of America’s most famous journalists.
It also helped start a new style of reporting called investigative journalism.
Later, after reading the famous book Around the World in 80 Days, Bly decided to break the world record for the fastest trip around the world.
Completing the trip in just 72 days, she set the record and then wrote a book about the experience.
Today, Bly is remembered as both an important journalist and a brave woman.

sets.name: Section 03 Reading 4 수능:ON 도표
sents: The tables above show the number of Korean and foreign visitors to Korean palaces in 2023 and 2024.
For the two-year period of 2023 to 2024, the overall total number of visitors to Deoksugung Palace was larger than that to Changgyeonggung Palace.
While the number of Korean visitors to Changgyeonggung Palace decreased from 2023 to 2024, the number of Korean visitors to Deoksugung Palace increased during the same period.
During both 2023 and 2024, the two palaces had more Korean visitors than foreign visitors.
In 2023, the number of foreign visitors to Changgyeonggung Palace made up only about 10 percent of the total visitors that year.
In 2024, the number of Korean visitors to Deoksugung Palace was more than 10 times the number of foreign visitors.

sets.name: Section 04 Reading 1 끈 떨어진 우주 비행사
sents: In the film Gravity, two astronauts accidentally drift off into space when the rope that attaches their spacesuits to their spacecraft breaks while they are on a spacewalk.
Among astronauts, this situation is called “going overboard.”
If this really happened, the astronauts would float away helplessly.
Since they would be completely weightless, kicking and waving wouldn’t help them change direction.
They wouldn’t be able to get back to their spacecraft and might end up descending toward Earth, eventually burning up in the atmosphere.
For this reason, NASA makes all astronauts wear a special emergency jetpack called SAFER.
First, the jetpack stops the astronauts from spinning around and around, and then it provides them with the ability to navigate through space.
The jetpack has three pounds of fuel, and astronauts are equipped with enough oxygen to breathe for seven and a half hours.
With these jetpacks, astronauts can return safely to the spacecraft!

sets.name: Section 04 Reading 2 들어올 순 있어도, 나갈 순 없다
sents: How do hospitals stop the spread of infectious diseases among patients, despite being full of germs?
The answer lies in negative pressure rooms, which were widely used during the COVID-19 pandemic.
But what exactly are these rooms, and how do they operate?
The purpose of negative pressure rooms is to maintain a lower air pressure inside the room compared to the surrounding areas.
This is achieved through a specially-designed ventilation system, which includes exhaust fans, intake vents, and air pressure monitors.
The exhaust fans steadily remove air from the closed-off room, creating a vacuum effect.
As a result, when a door is opened or a breach occurs, air from the surrounding environment is pulled into the room to equalize the pressure, preventing contaminants from spreading to other spaces.
For negative pressure rooms to be effective, several key design features are necessary.
Air pressure monitors are needed to continuously measure and display the pressure difference between the room and its surroundings.
Additionally, high-efficiency particulate air (HEPA) filters must be used.
Being able to capture at least 99.97% of particles as small as 0.3 micrometers, these advanced filters are essential to trapping bacteria and viruses.
To maintain low pressure, these rooms must also be tightly sealed, with secure doors, windows, and openings.

sets.name: Section 04 Reading 3 가까워질수록 높아지는 것들
sents: While you’re walking down a street, you hear a fire truck’s siren.
How interesting that it sounds higher-pitched as it approaches and lower as it moves away.
This is the Doppler Effect, first explained by Christian Doppler in 1842.
It is the change in wave frequency as the observer and source move relative to each other.
If sources have higher frequencies, they produce higher pitches; lower frequencies produce lower pitches.
When the fire truck approaches, its sound waves are squeezed, increasing the frequency, and ultimately, the pitch.
Conversely, as it moves away, the waves travel farther to reach your ears, resulting in stretched waves, and ultimately, a lower pitch.
The Doppler Effect applies not only to sound but also to light.
When an object moves away from us, the light waves stretch, causing a shift toward the red end of the spectrum, also known as redshift.
On the other hand, blueshift occurs when the compressed waves of an approaching object move toward the blue end of the spectrum.
Astronomers apply these shifts to understand the movement of objects in space, making it crucial for charting the universe.
The Doppler Effect can help us make sense of everyday experiences as well as complex scientific research.

sets.name: Section 04 Reading 4 수능:ON 짧은 어구 빈칸 추론
sents: Fishing nets are commonly used in the ocean.
But did you know they can also be used in space?
The Earth’s orbit is full of junk.
In fact, scientists estimate that there are 370,000 pieces of space debris up there.
There is a concern that a piece of junk might crash into a satellite.
A crash would result in thousands more pieces of debris, possibly destroying other satellites.
This could be a big problem, as we rely on satellites for many important things, like GPS, international phone connections, television signals, and weather forecasts.
To deal with this, Japanese space scientists and a 100-year-old fishing net company came up with a brilliant idea.
They will attach a thin metal fishing net to a satellite and then launch the satellite into space.
Once the satellite is in orbit, the net will be released to collect space junk.
Several weeks later the net, charged with electricity, will be pulled down by the Earth’s magnetic field.
The net and the junk will burn up as they enter the Earth’s atmosphere.
In this way, a simple fishing net will make space much cleaner and safer!

sets.name: Section 05 Reading 1 딱 한 번만 팔았을 뿐인데
sents: A confident new employee at the region’s largest department store told his manager at the beginning of his first shift, “I’m the world’s greatest salesperson.”
The manager laughed skeptically and replied, “We shall see.”
At closing time, when the manager inquired how many sales the man had made, he replied that he had made a single sale.
The manager turned red with rage and shouted that most of the other employees had made dozens of sales worth hundreds of dollars.
The man winked and explained that his one sale was worth $50,000.
“Fifty thousand dollars?” gasped the astonished manager.
“How is that possible?”
“Well, first I sold the customer a fishing rod, along with some expensive fishing gear.
Then, after I informed him that the biggest fish are in the middle of the lake, I sold him a new speedboat.
And since he was worried that his vehicle wasn’t powerful enough to tow the boat, I sold him a new four-wheel-drive SUV.”
“You’re kidding!
A customer wanted to purchase a fishing rod, and you sold him all that?” asked the manager.
“Actually, he came in to buy some aspirin, and I convinced him that fishing is the best remedy for a headache,” answered the employee.

sets.name: Section 05 Reading 2 라면 왕, 노르웨이를 사로잡다
sents: As a child, Chul-Ho Lee was badly injured during the Korean War.
To receive treatment, he was sent to Norway.
After he recovered, he stayed in Norway, where he eventually became a king—not the actual king of Norway, of course, but Norway’s “Ramen King.”
He started out working as a dishwasher at a hotel, but he quickly acquired cooking skills.
After receiving a cooking license, he became a chef at a popular hotel.
In 1968, Lee returned to Korea for a visit.
While he was there, he tasted ramen for the first time.
He thought it was delicious, so he wanted to introduce it to Norwegians.
In 1989, he began importing ramen to Norway, but people found it excessively spicy for their taste.
So Lee began to experiment with different styles until he developed a mild flavor that Norwegians enjoyed, which he then used to establish his own brand, known as Mr. Lee.
Now, nearly 80% of the ramen sold in Norway is Mr. Lee Ramen.
Chul-Ho Lee’s story shows how someone can go from a scared and injured child to an extremely successful businessman.
So next time you feel discouraged, remember the Ramen King of Norway.
If he could succeed despite his struggles, so can you!

sets.name: Section 05 Reading 3 당신의 간식이 작아지는 진짜 이유
sents: At least once, you might have eaten a snack and wondered, “Wasn’t this bigger before?”
Perhaps your bag of chips felt lighter, or your favorite candy bar seemed smaller than you remember.
If so, you’re not alone, and it’s not your imagination playing tricks on you.
This phenomenon, known as “shrinkflation,” is a subtle way in which companies manage higher costs and boost profits.
While most people are familiar with inflation, which is characterized by price increases, shrinkflation is its strategic variation.
Rather than raising prices, companies reduce the size or quantity of a product.
Shrinkflation is frequently viewed as a deceptive strategy because consumers are usually unaware of the reduced product size and are misled by the perceived price stability.
However, if consumers notice, they are likely to feel cheated.
So is shrinkflation legal?
Currently, there are no specific laws prohibiting it.
The only requirement for manufacturers is to clearly display the product’s weight or volume on the front of the packaging, though consumers can easily overlook this information while shopping.
So next time you’re shopping, don’t just glance at the price—check the size and quantity as well.
Being mindful of product sizes can facilitate smarter decision-making and prevent you from getting the short end of the stick.

sets.name: Section 05 Reading 4 수능:ON 무관한 문장
sents: The overabundance of options in today’s marketplace gives you more freedom of choice.
However, there may be a price to pay in terms of happiness.
According to research by psychologists David Myers and Robert Lane, having too many choices often makes people depressed.
Researchers gave some shoppers 24 choices of jams to taste and others only 6 choices.
Those who had fewer choices were happier with the tasting.
Even more surprisingly, the ones with a smaller selection purchased jam 31% of the time, while those with a wider range of choices only purchased jam 3% of the time.
The ironic thing about this is that people nearly always say they want more choices.
Yet, the more options they have, the more paralyzed they become.
Savvy business owners know to provide their customers with fewer choices.
This allows customers to feel more relaxed, prompting easier decisions and leaving them more satisfied with their choices.

sets.name: Section 06 Reading 1 손이 모자라? 해결 완료!
sents: Imagine that you need to carry a lot of items but your hands aren’t big enough to hold everything.
If only you had an extra hand.
While we can’t grow new body parts, researchers at the University of Cambridge have developed an innovative solution: the Third Thumb.
This robotic thumb was developed to boost the function of the hand.
The Third Thumb is worn on the side of the palm next to the pinky and resembles a sixth finger.
Wireless sensors on each wearer’s big toes signal the Thumb to move when pressed down.
The right toe moves the Thumb across the palm, while the left toe moves it toward the fingers.
The amount of pressure applied by the toes determines the Thumb’s strength, and the speed of their movement controls its quickness.
British product designer, Dani Clode and researchers at Cambridge University created the Third Thumb hoping to provide a tool for people who need extra assistance.
These include people with disabilities, such as paralysis, and reduced functioning caused by injuries and conditions.
Surgeons and dental hygienists, for example, would also find it useful because they could handle more devices in their hands.
The Third Thumb can help people regain their motor skills and more efficiently complete everyday tasks.
This incredible tool pushes the boundaries between technology and the human body.

sets.name: Section 06 Reading 2 수술실에 울려 퍼진 음악 소리
sents: While a team of doctors operates on his brain, a patient hums songs and plays the saxophone.
This unusual situation actually happened in 2016.
The patient was a 25-year-old musician named Dan Fabbio.
Fabbio had a tumor located in the part of the brain involved in making and listening to music.
Doctors hoped to remove it without affecting Fabbio’s musical abilities, so they spent months making a three-dimensional map of his brain.
While the doctors performed MRI scans on his brain, Fabbio listened to songs and hummed them.
This helped the doctors locate the parts of his brain related to music.
Although the map was useful, the cautious doctors decided to keep Fabbio awake during the surgery, asking him to hum songs occasionally.
This activity showed the doctors exactly which areas of the brain to avoid.
Toward the end of the operation, they decided to give Fabbio a test.
They brought his saxophone into the operating room and had him play a song on it.
He played the song perfectly, and the doctors and nurses happily applauded his performance.
In the end, the surgery was a great success.
The tumor was removed, and Fabbio didn’t lose his musical talent!

sets.name: Section 06 Reading 3 제로 칼로리의 함정
sents: These days, it’s common to see zero-calorie drinks advertised in supermarkets.
These diet-friendly beverages maintain the same sweet taste as their sugary counterparts but contain considerably fewer calories.
Although they seem beneficial for weight loss, did you know that they may have the opposite effect?
The food industry promotes zero-calorie drinks as a healthier alternative to traditional soda, but in reality, they can negatively impact normal bodily functions.
The sweetness in these drinks comes from artificial sweeteners like aspartame, which is around 200 times sweeter than regular white sugar.
Studies have shown that such sweeteners stimulate appetite and lead to higher consumption of foods containing an excessive amount of fat and calories.
These sweeteners also disrupt the release of satiety hormones, which regulate hunger by signaling the brain to stop eating.
Consequently, people who consume drinks that contain artificial sweeteners feel compelled to increase their food intake to alleviate their appetite.
Over time, cravings for sweet and fatty foods can contribute to weight gain and conditions like diabetes, a disease where the body cannot regulate the sugar in the blood properly.
So, if you regularly consume zero-calorie drinks, understand that they carry risks just like traditional sodas.

sets.name: Section 06 Reading 4 수능:ON 글의 순서
sents: Jack Andraka was just 15 years old when a close friend of his family died of pancreatic cancer.
Motivated by this tragedy, he conducted some research and learned that pancreatic cancer is usually found too late.
If it were found early, the patient’s chance of survival would be much higher.
Unfortunately, the tools used to detect pancreatic cancer were expensive and unreliable.
Even though he was just a teenager, Jack decided to do something about this.
He started by contacting 200 medical professionals to seek assistance.
However, he was rejected 199 times.
Just when Jack was about to give up, a doctor at Johns Hopkins School of Medicine agreed to be his mentor.
Using the doctor’s lab, Jack carefully examined 8,000 proteins found in human blood.
Finally, after endless hours of hard work, he discovered what he was searching for—a protein that revealed pancreatic cancer even in its earliest stages.
Jack used this protein to create a new test for diagnosing pancreatic cancer that costs just three cents, takes five minutes, and is nearly 100% accurate.
For his amazing work, Jack was named the winner of the Intel International Science & Engineering Fair, but more importantly, he invented something that has the potential to save countless lives.

sets.name: Section 07 Reading 1 역대 가장 똑똑한 의사
sents: The human brain is an extraordinary thing.
However, there are some tasks that are simply too intricate for our brains to handle well.
That’s why artificial intelligence, also known as AI, plays many crucial roles, especially in the field of healthcare.
Doctors in the US are highly trained and have access to all the latest equipment.
Despite this, it is estimated that American doctors make about 1.5 million medication mistakes every year.
This isn’t always the doctor’s fault.
If you wanted to read every new medical paper that was published, you would need 160 hours of free time every week.
In reality, most doctors spend five hours a month or less reading medical papers.
AI, on the other hand, has the ability to analyze and comprehend every medical paper ever written, and all of these details can be stored in a database and recalled instantly.
Using this information, it can recommend medications and treatments just as well as the best doctors, and it is less likely to make errors.
Of course, there is a downside in that AI cannot show concern or care like humans can.
Patients need proper treatments and medications, but they also need compassion.
For this reason, AI will never completely replace human doctors, though we should still take advantage of AI to reduce errors within the healthcare system.

sets.name: Section 07 Reading 2 도심 속 작은 오아시스
sents: Unlike most parks, the High Line in New York City does not feature sports fields, playgrounds, or a running track.
It is not even found at street level; rather, it is located high above the streets, weaving through buildings in Manhattan.
Originally constructed as a train line, the High Line replaced a street that was once known as “Death Avenue,” where a number of people were involved in train-related accidents.
To minimize accidents, the tracks were elevated onto a structure that was ten meters high.
However, the line experienced a decline in usage over time, and in 1980, trains stopped using the line altogether.
With concerns regarding the abandoned structure, the city proposed to tear it down.
In response, Robert Hammond, a local designer, established an organization called Friends of the High Line in order to preserve it.
Its members tried to think of a new use for the structure.
Upon visiting the tracks, Hammond discovered the structure was covered in beautiful wildflowers, inspiring him to transform it into a park.
Initially, his idea was opposed due to the significant cost of converting the space into a park.
However, Hammond emphasized the benefits the park could offer the community, and eventually, the city government approved of the project.
The park’s first section opened to the public in 2009.
In the subsequent year, it attracted more than two million visitors.
With a little imagination and some hard effort, an old railway line was turned into a distinctive public space.

sets.name: Section 07 Reading 3 앙카라의 헌책 도서관
sents: What happens to old books when their owners don’t want them anymore?
Sadly, many of them are tossed into the trash.
Sanitation workers in Ankara, Turkey, noticed this, so they began to rescue the books and bring them back to the sanitation department’s headquarters.
As their collection grew larger and larger, these thoughtful workers decided to put the books to good use.
Working together, they created their own library.
At first it was only used by their friends and families, but soon they opened it to the public.
Located in their headquarters, the library includes more than 50,000 books, including textbooks, comic books, children’s books, science fiction novels, and more!
The library even includes a lounge, where local people can drink tea, play chess, or just sit back and enjoy a good book.
Today, the library continues to expand and has become an essential part of the local community.
People now donate their unwanted books directly to the library, and thanks to the local government, it also has a full-time librarian now.
There are even plans to convert an old garbage truck into a mobile library, which will be driven around the city and to nearby villages, bringing books to people who need them.
All of this began with some sanitation workers who didn’t want to see books go to waste.
Together, they showed the world that anyone can take action and make their community a better place.

sets.name: Section 07 Reading 4 수능:ON 문장 삽입
sents: Socks are just something we pull onto our feet every morning, so they may not seem important to you and me.
But they can make a huge difference in the lives of some people.
Adina Lichtman learned this when she was a college student.
She had decided to help homeless people in New York City and was distributing free sandwiches on the street.
One grateful man thanked her for the sandwich, but then he mentioned that winter was coming.
When the weather turns frigid, he told her, homeless people need socks more than anything else.
That night, after deciding to take action, Lichtman started knocking on doors in her dormitory, asking her classmates to donate one pair of socks.
By the next morning, she had collected 40 pairs.
Today she runs a nonprofit organization, called Knock Knock, Give a Sock (KKGS), that has donated more than 3,000,000 pairs of socks to homeless people all across America.

There are numerous organizations that work to help the homeless, but Lichtman explains why KKGS is special: “While many people donate clothing, nine out of every ten clothing donors have never donated socks.”
Lichtman discovered an important need and found a way to fill it.
Thanks to her innovative thinking, thousands of people will have warm feet this winter.

sets.name: Section 08 Reading 1 입 안에서 자라는 생명
sents: Birds build nests for their eggs, while mammals nurse their newborns.
Nurturing methods vary across species, but the parenting of East African lake cichlids is unique.
Cichlids, which are a type of freshwater fish, hold their offspring in their mouths —they are mouthbrooders!
Male cichlids begin by digging a pit or nest in the ground to provide a suitable place for the female to lay her eggs.
Once the eggs are laid, the male fertilizes them.
Subsequently, she carefully gathers them in her mouth.
It takes 10-15 days for the eggs to hatch, during which time she cannot eat, inevitably leading to a period of starvation.
After hatching, she will continue to hold them in her mouth for up to two additional weeks.
She only releases them so they can feed, but she will grab them if she detects danger.
So why do female cichlids keep their eggs in their mouth?
Newly hatched cichlids, being small and vulnerable, are easily targeted by predators.
Mouthbrooding offers protection from predators, such as other cichlids.
By nurturing their offspring in their mouths, cichlids can significantly enhance their offspring’s chances for survival.
Cichlids have evolved to raise their offspring effectively and safely.
This parental strategy shows the strong sense of their maternal instinct.

sets.name: Section 08 Reading 2 숫자를 세는 식물
sents: The Venus flytrap is well-known for catching insects by shutting its jaw-like lobes in the blink of an eye.
This is possible because three trigger hairs on each lobe detect movement in the trap.
When at least two of the three trigger hairs are touched, the trap snaps shut.
But did you know this process is based on the Venus flytrap’s ability to count?
On the first touch, the trigger hairs transmit a bio-electrical signal that serves as an indicator —it doesn’t cause the trap to close.
The plant will instead wait to confirm if it was a valid trigger.
The second stimulus activates the trap and snaps it shut in under a second, subsequently releasing the hormone jasmonate, which activates digestive enzymes.
Five or more signals boost enzyme production in the plant’s 37,000 glands and activate transport molecules to absorb the digested insects.
The bigger the prey, the more fiercely it struggles, which further stimulates the trigger hairs, increasing digestive enzyme production.
This process exhibits how Venus flytraps utilize a short-term memory mechanism.
In essence, the plant must remember the first stimulus until the second stimulus is triggered, demonstrating its remarkable ability to count the number of stimuli.

sets.name: Section 08 Reading 3 사마귀 귀의 비밀
sents: Praying mantises are elusive creatures.
But if you look carefully, you may find one hidden in your garden, though they are nearly invisible amongst plant leaves and stems.
Interestingly, mantises have five eyes, including three small, simple eyes and two large compound eyes.
What’s more surprising is that they have only one ear, which can be found on their chest between their back legs!
Animals with two ears can identify differences in the timing and intensity of the sounds reaching each ear.
This information is used to estimate the direction and distance of the sounds.
With only one ear, mantises don’t have this capability.
So what does a mantis’s ear do?
Despite its limitations, the ear plays a vital role in detecting life threatening situations.
It has the ability to detect ultrasonic waves such as the sounds emitted by bats, one of the mantis’ primary predators.
As soon as a mantis senses a bat, which it can do from up to 10 meters away, it immediately dives toward the ground to avoid capture.
The unique position of the mantis’ ear allows the mantis to quickly detect sound vibrations and react to danger.
Though the mantis’ single ear may seem strange, it is crucial to their survival.

sets.name: Section 08 Reading 4 수능:ON 긴 어구 빈칸 추론
sents: Can you imagine camels roaming across vast snow-covered landscapes?
It sounds strange, but this occurrence was likely normal millions of years ago.
Scientists recently discovered the bones of ancient camels in the Arctic region of Canada.
Apparently, this is where they lived long, long ago.
Interestingly, similar camel bones have been found about 1,200 kilometers to the south, indicating that these remarkable mammals migrated south.
About seven or eight million years ago, North America and Asia were connected, so the camels could simply walk from one continent to the other.
After a long journey, they eventually made their way to desert regions.
The fact that the camel migrated suggests that its evolution may have been influenced more by the Arctic than by the desert.
Its hump would have allowed it to store food during the dark, frozen winter months, and its broad feet would have made it easier to walk across the snow without sinking in.
Of course, these features were extremely useful when the camel switched to a desert habitat.

sets.name: Section 09 Reading 1 첫인상의 오류
sents: Imagine you’re looking for nutritious food at the supermarket.
You see two granola bars: one is labeled “organic,” and the other is not.
You will probably be inclined to choose the organic granola bar, assuming it’s a better choice.
However, many of these “health foods” still contain excessive amounts of sugar, contradicting your expectations.
This phenomenon is called the halo effect.
The halo effect is the tendency to make an overall judgment—either positive or negative—based on a single characteristic.
It is a form of cognitive bias that causes you to make quick decisions while ignoring key information.
It might seem beneficial to make decisions faster, but it also puts you at risk of making the wrong choice.
Relying too much on first impressions can interfere with your judgment.
For instance, you might believe that your coworker is a respected leader because they graduated from a prestigious university.
However, an impressive college degree doesn’t guarantee good leadership.
In reality, they might struggle to take on a leadership role, and your bias may prove to be misleading.
This exemplifies how the halo effect is unconscious, meaning it influences your decision-making when you don’t realize it.
Therefore, you should be cautious about judging anything without considering all the available information.

sets.name: Section 09 Reading 2 꿈을 꾸고 있어요
sents: Dreams can be captivating, exciting, or even scary, and most of the time, they occur without conscious control.
But occasionally, we experience extraordinary dreams.
Not only do we realize that we are dreaming, but we can also control what happens!
These are referred to as lucid dreams.
In typical dreams, self-awareness is generally absent, whereas during lucid dreams, the brain seems to show activity associated with being awake.
In this heightened state of consciousness, we can navigate our dream environment, as if completely awake.
Additionally, while ordinary dreams usually fade after waking and stay in our memory for only a short time, lucid dreams often remain vivid and memorable after we have awakened.
Nevertheless, lucid dreams present certain drawbacks.
First, they can be exhausting, as they disrupt normal sleep cycles, preventing us from getting adequate rest.
Furthermore, lucid dreaming has the potential to become a habitual behavior, one that people find difficult to resist.
There are those who believe that lucid dreams are more than just an interesting experience and say that these dreams can lead to personal development.
Individuals might be able to use them to gain confidence and overcome their fears, so a person who is hesitant to attempt something in real life can confront it first in their dreams!

sets.name: Section 09 Reading 3 메기가 나타나면
sents: Sardine fishermen encountered a dilemma: sardines were dying quickly after being caught, but live sardines could be sold at a higher price.
So, one fisherman came up with a brilliant solution.
He introduced a catfish into each container of captured sardines.
To avoid this predator, they were forced to keep swimming around, and this constant movement kept them alive longer.
This phenomenon, called the catfish effect can be applied to situations in various fields.
In sports, for example, coaches understand that bringing a new, talented player onto a team enhances the performance of the other players.
This happens because players start playing harder to avoid losing their position on the team.
Similarly, businesses utilize this effect to motivate their employees.
In economics, the effect explains how companies can foster creativity and innovation.
The entering of strong competitors in the market pressures other companies to become more adaptable to survive, causing the entire economy to become stronger.
In short, pressure and stimulation caused by the introduction of a competitor or threat can make people and businesses work harder.

sets.name: Section 09 Reading 4 수능:ON 함의 추론
sents: Over the centuries, various writers and thinkers, looking at humans from an outside perspective, have been struck by the theatrical quality of social life.

The most famous quote expressing this comes from Shakespeare: “All the world’s a stage, And all the men and women merely players; They have their exits and their entrances, And one man in his time plays many parts.”
If the theater and actors were traditionally represented by the image of masks, writers such as Shakespeare are implying that all of us are constantly wearing masks.
Some people are better actors than others.
Evil types such as Iago in the play Othello are able to conceal their hostile intentions behind a friendly smile.
Others are able to act with more confidence and bravado—they often become leaders.
People with excellent acting skills can better navigate our complex social environments and get ahead.

sets.name: Section 10 Reading 1 내가 모델이 된다고?
sents: A stylish woman poses on the street, and a man takes a picture of her.
You might think she is a model or celebrity, but she is not.
She is just an ordinary but fashionable woman in her own clothes, and the photographer is Scott Schuman, one of the world’s most-famous fashion photographers.
After quitting his fashion sales job in 2005, Schuman went to the streets with his digital camera and spent four to five hours a day photographing people’s street wear.
His target was anyone dressed attractively.
It didn’t matter if they were wearing trendy clothes or expensive brands.
Then he posted the photos to his blog, The Sartorialist.

The blog gained international attention because people found his pictures different from typical fashion photos, and millions of people from different backgrounds started visiting his blog to get style inspiration.
Soon after, famous brands began collaborating with him on advertising campaigns, and magazines started running his pictures.
Schuman believes individuality is the most important thing in fashion.
To him, a well-dressed person is one who displays a personal style, rather than a manufactured look created by stylists.

sets.name: Section 10 Reading 2 과일인가 사람인가
sents: What do you see when you observe this painting?
At first glance, it seems to depict a simple bowl filled with various vegetables.
However, when turned upside down, a different picture can be perceived.
The bowl transforms into a hat, and the vegetables form the shape of a man’s smiling face.
This unique style of painting was pioneered by Giuseppe Arcimboldo, a prominent artist of the Renaissance.
During this period, artists typically painted either objects or portraits.
Arcimboldo ingeniously combined these two styles, arranging the objects in his paintings to resemble people’s faces.
Viewing his paintings from a distance, they may be perceived as human figures.
But, upon closer inspection, a collection of objects, such as flowers, books, or animals can be discovered.
Despite Arcimboldo being famous during his lifetime, his work faded from the public’s attention following his death in the sixteenth century.
However, his remarkable artwork gained popularity once again in the twentieth century.
His innovative method of combining many objects to create the peculiar appearance of a person served as inspiration for later surrealist painters like Salvador Dali.

sets.name: Section 10 Reading 3 스타들의 숨겨진 과거
sents: At times, it seems like celebrities have no challenges, doesn’t it?
They’re famous and charismatic, but they sometimes encounter obstacles, too.
You may be startled to learn that many celebrities have learning disabilities, and the following is a list of inspirational stars who have learned to live with a disability.
Bruce Willis is a retired actor praised for his acting ability, but he wasn’t initially natural on camera.
Until he reached the age of twenty, he struggled with a stuttering problem.
In an interview, he revealed that acting helped him beat his stutter and work on his sense of humor.
By being funny, Willis was able to keep people’s attention off his disability and on his comedic acting skills.
American swimmer Michael Phelps is fast and agile in the pool.
But Phelps’ focus wasn’t always strong, as he had ADHD.
In school, Phelps sometimes got in trouble for not sitting still in class.
But when he turned his attention to swimming, he was able to build his concentration.
After years of training, his persistent hard work ultimately resulted in multiple Olympic gold medals.
When Keira Knightley was young, her classmates teased her because she could not read.
It turned out that she had dyslexia.
To help her defeat her disability, Knightley’s parents made a deal with her.
They agreed to find her an acting agent if she learned to read.
Well, you can probably imagine how it turned out, because Knightley is now one of the most renowned actresses in the world.

sets.name: Section 10 Reading 4 수능:ON 요약문
sents: Everyone enjoys watching the track and field events at the Olympics.
Understandably, the focus is only on how fast the athletes are running, but there’s something else most people probably don’t notice.
In all the events, the athletes run in a counterclockwise direction.
Why is that?
Firstly, it is related to the structure of the human body, specifically, the position of the heart, the body’s most vital organ, which is slightly to the left of the center.
When a runner turns to the left in a counterclockwise direction, he or she encounters centrifugal force.
On a left-hand turn, centrifugal force pushes to the right and helps the heart to pump blood more easily to the other organs in the body.
This increase in blood circulation means the runner does not tire too quickly.
Turning to the right has the opposite effect, as blood is pushed to the left and away from the other organs.
The other key point is that turning to the left is more natural for most people because the act requires the right foot to push harder.
Just as most people are right-handed, most also have a stronger right foot, so turning left is an easier motion.
Next time you visit an athletics track, try running around it in a clockwise direction.
You’ll feel how much more difficult it is, and understand why we normally run the other way!
